title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is Grothendieck's handwritten sketch of an axiomatic 'théorie de l'orientation des variétés topologiques'. It is the programme carried out in M. Wanderley's thèse de 3e cycle (Montpellier, 1980), summarised in the CRAS note of 1981 reproduced on the previous page.

Setting. V̄ is the category of topological manifolds with boundary, with open immersions as morphisms. V is the full subcategory of manifolds without boundary. There are two functors V̄ → V:
- ∂, the topological boundary;
- Int, X ↦ X − ∂X, the interior.
V̄_{≤n}, V_{≤n}, V̄_n, V_n are the subcategories of dimension ≤ n, respectively pure dimension n.

Data of an orientation theory.
- (i) A presheaf Ω on V (a functor V^op → Ens), with Ω_n its restriction to V_n. Ω(X) is meant to be 'the set of orientations of X'.
- (ii) A distinguished element ω⁺ ∈ Ω(e), where e is the one-point manifold.
- (iii) A natural transformation of functors on V̄^op, Ω(Int X) → Ω(∂X). This is the abstract 'Stokes / outward-normal' rule inducing boundary orientations.

Axioms.
- 1°) Ω is a sheaf on the big site of manifolds: for every X, the restriction Ω_X to the open sets of X is a sheaf, the orientation sheaf of X. A crossed-out remark wanted the Ω_X to be étale double covers. The margin note 'vérif. locale' says that this property should be checked locally.
- 2°) card Ω(e) = 2. The other element is ω⁻, and ω^± ↦ ±1 identifies Ω(e) with {±1} ⊂ ℤ, the multiplicity of an oriented point. A margin note says this is the 'starting hypothesis of the induction (construction of Ω)'. The idea is that Ω_n is built from Ω_{n−1} through the boundary map (iii), starting from points.

From this data one gets a category V^(Ω) of Ω-oriented manifolds.

Codimension-one construction. Take Y ⊂ X, a codimension-1 submanifold. Locally Y has two 'rives' (sides), giving a sheaf ρ_{Y/X} that is an étale double cover, i.e. the local co-orientations of Y. Choosing a side makes Y, locally, the boundary of a manifold with boundary whose interior is open in X. Datum (iii) then sends Ω(X) into Hom(ρ_{Y/X}, Ω_Y). Sheafifying gives Ω_X|Y → Hom(ρ_{Y/X}, Ω_Y), equivalently a pairing Ω_X|Y × ρ_{Y/X} → Ω_Y.

In modern terms this is the canonical isomorphism of μ₂-torsors or-sheaf(Y) ≅ or-sheaf(X)|_Y ⊗ (normal co-orientation sheaf). It is the topological analogue of 'or(TX|_Y) = or(N) ⊗ or(TY)'.

Purpose. Characterise orientations intrinsically, by universal sheaf-theoretic properties on the big site of manifolds. The published outcome (Wanderley) is:
- 'separated' sheaves on V_m are locally constant;
- locally constant sheaves on V_m are equivalent to Π(m)-sets, with Π(m) the group completion of the monoid of injective continuous self-maps of ℝ^m;
- Stokes triples are equivalent to Π(m)-sets;
- Π(m) ≅ μ₂ is equivalent to the stable homeomorphism conjecture, hence true for m ≠ 4 by Kirby.
errors: The text says ρ_{Y/X} is 'un rev. étale d'ordre 2 de X'. It should be a double cover of Y, since sides are defined along Y. Only in a tubular neighbourhood can it be read as living near Y in X.
Minor typing slip: X is taken in Ob V̄ (with boundary) while Ω_X is defined for X in V. Implicitly one should use Int X, or require Y to lie in the interior.

Hypotheses are left unstated: existence of local collars or bicollars for Y, i.e. local flatness of Y. Without them the 'rives' sheaf need not be a double cover (wild codimension-1 embeddings, e.g. Alexander horned sphere phenomena). The CRAS axioms handle this through the 'isomorphisme local' condition.

ideas.what: Orientation as a sheaf on the big site of topological manifolds with open immersions, normalised by card Ω(point)=2
ideas.modern_name: Tangential structure as a (locally constant) sheaf on Mfld_n / Disk_n; orientation sheaf as μ₂-torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical orientation sheaf: Leray/Godement/Borel–Moore; big-site/sheaf-on-Mfld_n viewpoint: Weiss, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Lurie (2000s). Axiomatic version here: Wanderley 1980/81
ideas.where_published: Wanderley, thèse 3e cycle Montpellier 1980; C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 292 (1981)

ideas.what: Natural transformation Ω(Int X) → Ω(∂X) as abstract 'Stokes' boundary-orientation rule; 'Stokes triples'
ideas.modern_name: Boundary orientation convention (outward normal first) axiomatised; compatibility of tangential structures with boundary

ideas.what: Sheaf of 'rives' (sides) of a codimension-1 submanifold and the pairing Ω_X|Y × ρ_{Y/X} → Ω_Y
ideas.modern_name: or(Y) ≅ or(X)|_Y ⊗ or(normal bundle); co-orientation double cover

ideas.what: Construction of Ω by induction on dimension, starting from the point and passing through boundaries
ideas.modern_name: Inductive determination of orientation via boundary/Stokes data

missed.claim: This page documents that the axiomatic orientation theory published under Wanderley's name (thesis 1980, CRAS 1981) was laid out by Grothendieck himself. That includes the big-site sheaf formulation and the boundary transformation. Grothendieck's role as originator of this programme is not generally recorded.
missed.quote: Une théorie de l'orientation des variétés topologiques consiste en (i) Un foncteur Ω : V^0 → (Ens) ... (iii) Un homm. de foncteurs sur V̄^0 Ω(int X) → Ω(∂X)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical attribution point about Grothendieck's Montpellier-era supervision and his interest in topological manifolds via topos-like 'gros sites'.

missed.claim: The programme treats orientations as locally constant sheaves on the big site of n-manifolds with open embeddings, classified by the group completion of the monoid of self-embeddings of ℝ^n. This anticipates the modern view: tangential structures are presheaves on Disk_n/Mfld_n, governed by Emb(ℝ^n,ℝ^n) ≃ Top(n), as in factorization homology and the cobordism hypothesis. Moreover, Quinn's 1982 resolution of the stable homeomorphism conjecture in dimension 4 removes the m≠4 restriction in the companion result, giving Π(m) ≅ μ₂ for all m. That completion does not seem to be recorded in connection with this work.
missed.quote: Ω est un faisceau [i.e. ∀ X ∈ Ob V, la restriction Ω_X de Ω à la catégorie des ouverts de X est un faisceau]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, π₀-level instance of the 'sheaves on Mfld_n' formalism, and a small completable statement (all dimensions) for Wanderley's theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is the conceptual blueprint of a published (if obscure) thesis and CRAS note, so the mathematics is not unpublished. The modest interest lies in showing Grothendieck's authorship of the big-site axiomatic approach to orientation, which foreshadows later Mfld_n-sheaf viewpoints.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'V^*' is a marked symbol for the category of manifolds without boundary (sans bord); it is the same V used afterwards.
The superscript on ρ_{Y/X} is hard to read, roughly '(x'', ω)'; it is uncertain and probably not '(X,ω)'.
Margin notes beside 1°)-2°): 'vérif. locale' and 'hyp. de démarrage de récurrence (construction de Ω)' are correctly placed as marginalia.
Crossed-out text after 1°) reads approximately 'Ω_X → X sont revêtements étales d'ordre 2'.
